data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: aim
sections.question: aim
sections.summary: a goal or purpose; to try to achieve something

senses.definition: something you want to achieve; a goal or purpose
examples: Her aim is to pass all her exams with high marks this year.
The aim of the course is to improve your English.

senses.definition: to try to achieve something; to have something as a goal
examples: She aims to finish the project before the deadline.
He aimed to arrive at the office before nine o'clock.

answers.answer: Her aim is to pass all her exams with high marks this year.
He cooked an aim for dinner and served it with bread.
She bought two aims at the supermarket on Friday.
They planted an aim in the garden and watered it every day.

sections.title: am
sections.question: am
sections.summary: the first person singular present form of the verb 'be', used after 'I'

senses.definition: the first person singular present tense form of 'be'; used only after the subject 'I'
examples: I am very happy because today is my birthday.
I am a student at the local university.

answers.answer: I am very happy because today is my birthday.
She am very tired after the long train journey.
We am going to the cinema together tonight.
They am very talented students in the class.

sections.title: are
sections.question: are
sections.summary: the second person and plural present form of the verb 'be'

senses.definition: the present tense form of 'be', used after 'you', 'we', 'they', and plural nouns
examples: You are very good at speaking English.
The students are working hard because the exam is tomorrow.

answers.answer: The students are working hard because the exam is tomorrow.
I are very excited about the school trip.
She are a student at the local university.
He are my best friend from primary school.

sections.title: ate
sections.question: ate
sections.summary: past tense of eat; took food into the mouth and swallowed it

senses.definition: past tense of 'eat'; put food in the mouth and swallowed it
examples: She ate a big bowl of soup for lunch yesterday.
He ate all his dinner and asked for more.

answers.answer: She ate a big bowl of soup for lunch yesterday.
He ate his bicycle to school this morning.
She ate to the park and played football with her friends.
They ate very loudly through the city centre.

sections.title: bought
sections.question: bought
sections.summary: past tense of buy; paid money to get something

senses.definition: past tense of 'buy'; obtained something by paying money for it
examples: He bought some flowers for his mother on her birthday.
She bought a new coat because the weather was getting cold.

answers.answer: He bought some flowers for his mother on her birthday.
She bought to work by bus yesterday morning.
He bought very fast along the road to the station.
They bought in the swimming pool for an hour.

sections.title: decide
sections.question: decide
sections.summary: to make a choice between two or more possibilities

senses.definition: to think carefully about the different possibilities and choose one of them
examples: She decided to study abroad to improve her English.
He decided to leave early because the traffic was very bad.

answers.answer: She decided to study abroad to improve her English.
He decided his car to the school every morning.
She decided very quickly along the road to the market.
They decided their dinner with a knife and fork.

sections.title: dream
sections.question: dream
sections.summary: to have thoughts or images in your mind while sleeping; to wish for something

senses.definition: to have a series of thoughts and images in your mind while sleeping; to hope for or wish for something
examples: She dreams of travelling around the world one day.
He dreamed about being a pilot when he was a child.

senses.definition: a series of events or images that your mind creates while you sleep; something you hope for
examples: She had a very strange dream last night.
His dream is to become a professional footballer.

answers.answer: She dreams of becoming a doctor and helping people one day.
He dreamed his bicycle to school last Tuesday morning.
She dreams the weather outside every morning.
They dreamed dinner at home every evening.

sections.title: drove
sections.question: drove
sections.summary: past tense of drive; operated a vehicle and controlled its direction

senses.definition: past tense of 'drive'; operated a vehicle and controlled its direction and speed
examples: She drove her children to school because it was raining.
He drove to the airport early in the morning to catch his flight.

answers.answer: She drove her children to school because it was raining.
He drove a big dinner in the kitchen last night.
She drove very loudly at the party on Saturday evening.
They drove their homework before going to school.

sections.title: eat
sections.question: eat
sections.summary: to put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it

senses.definition: to put food into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it
examples: She likes to eat fresh fruit and vegetables every day.
He eats lunch at his desk because he is very busy.

answers.answer: She likes to eat fresh fruit and vegetables every day.
He eats his car to school every morning.
She eats very fast to the market on Saturday afternoon.
They eat the music every evening at the concert.

sections.title: expect
sections.question: expect
sections.summary: to think that something is likely to happen or that someone is likely to do something

senses.definition: to think that something is likely to happen or that someone will do something
examples: She expects to receive her exam results next week.
He expected the meeting to finish by lunchtime.

answers.answer: She expects to receive her exam results next week.
He expected his lunch with a fork and a knife.
She expects to school very quickly every morning.
They expected very loudly at the concert last night.
